subject: Investigation: BrightCart reported 'partial generation' — closure and recommended next steps
messages:
From: Alyssa Wang <alyssa@brightcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial output from `generate` endpoint (some runs)

Hi Monica,

We're seeing intermittent responses from Redwood's hosted inference that appear to stop mid-sentence — last ~30-60 tokens missing. This is happening across a handful of runs from two different services in our staging environment. Example: prompt attached (prompt_sample.txt) and a screenshot of the returned JSON (brightcart_screenshot.png).

Details:
- Endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (model: rwd-3b-v1)
- Request times: 2026-07-14T15:43:21Z, 2026-07-14T15:50:12Z
- Response body shows status 200 and truncated text. No obvious error in client logs.

Can you take a look? If you need a request id or traces I can share. This is blocking a QA pass.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Wang
Platform Engineer, BrightCart

Attachments: brightcart_screenshot.png (image/png), prompt_sample.txt (text)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Wang <alyssa@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial output from `generate` endpoint (some runs)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the report and the attachments. I'm Monica from Redwood support — I own BrightCart's account here.

Quick confirmation requests so we can scope this:
- Do you have the request IDs for the two runs you mentioned? If not, timestamps + client IP are fine.
- Which SDK/integration are you using (Python SDK, direct REST, custom streaming client)?
- Are you using max_tokens or a client-side cut-off?

I'll pull runtime traces and loop in our infra team. If it's helpful, we can also do a short screenshare to reproduce.

I might need permission to share a sanitized trace with engineering — please confirm.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Partial output from `generate` endpoint — BrightCart (staging)

Looping you both in on an incoming BrightCart issue. They reported two runs with truncated text; attached prompt and screenshot. I pulled a short runtime trace for the window they reported (redwood_trace_20260714.log attached). Summary of my quick repro attempts:
- Replayed the prompt against rwd-3b-v1 in our dev cluster with identical max_tokens/defaults — did not truncate.
- No server-side exceptions in the trace around the timestamps provided.
- I see several short client disconnects (RST) in the connection logs from a staging client IP range during the window — flagged but inconclusive.

Can you sanity-check the trace when you get a minute? Looking for: kernel crashes, abrupt process kill, or runtime returning an early EOF. If none, we should suspect a client-side streaming cutoff or an SDK-level max_tokens enforcement.

Attachments: redwood_trace_20260714.log

- Monica
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partial output from `generate` endpoint — BrightCart (staging)

Thanks for the trace, Monica. I reviewed redwood_trace_20260714.log and correlated it with host telemetry. Key findings: 
- No kernel or runtime crashes in that window.
- Model execution path completed and returned tokens up to the expected length; final token emission occurred ~2ms before the TCP FIN.
- There are multiple short TCP resets originating from BrightCart's staging IP range around the reported timestamps (confirmed by our edge logs). Those resets correlate with the times the client reported truncated content.
- No evidence of the runtime truncating generation mid-token. 

Recommendation: ask BrightCart to temporarily disable client-side timeouts/early stream termination and re-run. Also request they try an explicit larger max_tokens value (e.g., +128) to rule out SDK defaults. If they still see truncation, capture the raw request_id and earliest trace id so we can probe further.

I attached the small trace excerpt I pulled for your reference. Nothing server-side to indicate an incident.

- Sean
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Wang <alyssa@brightcart.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial output from `generate` endpoint (some runs)

Hi Alyssa — thank you for sending the samples. We completed a focused triage with our infra team and wanted to share the findings and recommended next steps.

Summary of investigation:
- We reviewed your provided artifacts and server-side traces for the times you reported. We were unable to reproduce a server-side generation truncation. Our runtime logs show the model produced the expected token stream and the process exited normally.
- The edge logs show short TCP resets originating from an IP in your staging CIDR at approximately the same times you saw truncated responses. The timing lines up with the client-side behaviour you described.
- No kernel faults, out-of-memory, or internal runtime exceptions were observed.

What we delivered back to you:
- A short redacted trace excerpt (redwood_trace_20260714.log) showing the successful token emission from the runtime.
- Observations from infra that indicate connection resets rather than server-side truncation.

Recommended actions for BrightCart (quick checklist):
1) Re-run the failing request with an explicit larger max_tokens (add +128) to rule out SDK defaults cutting output.
2) Disable any client-side streaming timeouts / auto-close logic during the retry.
3) If using a custom streaming client, try the official Redwood Python SDK or a single non-streaming REST call to compare.
4) If truncation persists, capture the full request_id (we can then surface the exact internal span) and share it with us.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll keep this thread open for 72 hours. If you can reproduce after trying the steps above, please send the request_id and we will escalate to a deeper trace and packet-level correlation (INF-2348).
- No customer-impacting server-side issue found in our environment at this time.
